title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning
location: Freeborn, MN; Steele, MN; Waseca, MN

details.description:
SVRMPX

The National Weather Service in the Twin Cities has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Freeborn County in south central Minnesota...
Southern Steele County in south central Minnesota...
Southeastern Waseca County in south central Minnesota...

* Until 745 AM CDT.

* At 700 AM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
13 miles north of Blooming Prairie to near New Richland, or along a
line from 12 miles east of Owatonna to 16 miles southwest of
Owatonna, moving southeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Otisco, Lemond, Hope, Rice Lake State Park, New Richland, Steele
Center, Ellendale, Bixby, Hartland, Blooming Prairie, Geneva,
Clarks Grove, Hollandale, Albert Lea Airport, Myre Big Island State
Park, Albert Lea, Hayward, Glenville, Myrtle and London.
details.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. These storms are capable of producing damaging winds and
large hail.

title: Special Weather Statement
location: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters

details.description:
Corrected typos and updated discussion.

...A DEVELOPING MONSOON PATTERN IS EXPECTED TO BRING HEAVY
DOWNPOURS...GUSTY WINDS...AND CHOPPY SEAS THE NEXT SEVERAL DAYS...

A developing monsoon pattern is producing fresh west-southwesterlies
and a surge of numerous to widespread locally heavy showers and
thunderstorms, accompanied by strong to near-gale gusts. There is
some indication that a monsoon disturbance may gradually form to the
north-northeast, which could lead to an intensified monsoon surge
across Palau and Yap. Model guidance suggests 3 to 5 inches through
the middle of the week, and an additional 2 to 4 inches through the
latter half of the week, totaling 6 to 9 inches by the weekend. If
these showers develop as expected, soils will become saturated enough
to pose a risk for mudslides toward the end of the week. At this
time, the risk remains low. As the monsoon pattern continues to
develop, winds and seas will increase, but are expected to remain
below conditions hazardous to small craft. As a tropical disturbance
embedded within the monsoon trough attempts to consolidate, it will
move north and carry the bulk of the convective monsoon with it,
easing the showers and winds near Palau and Yap as early as Saturday.

For more information, residents and mariners should monitor the
latest forecasts for the region at weather.gov/gum/PublicForecasts
and any information shared by WSO Palau and WSO Yap for their local
regions.

title: Heat Advisory
location: City of Hyder

details.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures up to 82 expected.

* WHERE...City of Hyder.

* WHEN...From 1 PM this afternoon to 7 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Individuals not accustomed to these unusually hot
temperatures for this region may experience heat related illnesses.
details.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside. Wear sunscreen and light loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Locations next to the ocean or glaciers will be cooler with a
stronger breeze in the afternoon.

title: Red Flag Warning
location: Morton; Grant; Sioux; Emmons

details.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM NOON CDT /11 AM MDT/ TODAY
TO 9 PM CDT /8 PM MDT/ THIS EVENING DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE
HUMIDITY FOR MORTON, GRANT, SIOUX, AND EMMONS COUNTIES...

.Critical fire weather conditions are expected in parts of south
central North Dakota this afternoon and early evening. Northwest
winds will increase to around 25 mph this afternoon, with gusts as
high as 40 mph. Relative humidity will fall as low as 20 percent this
afternoon as temperatures rise into the lower 90s. Any fires that
ignite will spread rapidly and become difficult to control.

* AFFECTED AREA...Morton, Grant, Sioux, and Emmons Counties.

* TIMING...From noon CDT /11 AM MDT/ today to 9 PM CDT /8 PM MDT/
this evening.

* WINDS...Northwest around 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 20 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that ignite will spread rapidly and become
difficult to control or suppress.
details.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute to
extreme fire behavior.

title: Special Weather Statement
location: North St. Louis; Northern Cook/Northern Lake; Central St. Louis

details.description:
Dry conditions and very strong west winds will lead to near
critical fire weather conditions today. West winds of 10 to 20
mph with gusts of 30 to 35 mph are forecast for the entire day
Minimum relative humidity values of 40 to 50 percent are also
expected, possibly drier in northern Saint Louis county where
overnight showers and storms only brough a few hundreths of an
inch of rain. Higher rainfall amounts did fall in northern Cook
and Lake Counties on the order of a quarter to half inch, but
skies will partially clear out quickly today leading to drying
condiitons. Together, these conditions could lead to the rapid
spread of fires. Check burning restrictions and fire danger before
burning.

For more information on burning restrictions for Minnesota, see
www.dnr.state.mn.us/forestry/fire/firerating_restrictions.html.

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee
River Fl out to 20 Nm...
Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM...

waterspouts were located along a line extending from 6 nm south of
St. Marks to 13 nm southwest of Suwannee River, moving north at 25
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Marker 24 Barge and Horseshoe Beach.
details.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

title: Heat Advisory
location: Southwest Highlands; Western Magic Valley; Southern Twin  Falls County

details.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures up to 100 expected.

* WHERE...Western Magic Valley, Southern Twin Falls County, and
Southwest Highlands.

* WHEN...From noon today to 9 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses, especially
for the young, elderly, and animals.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Warm overnight temperatures will limit
recovery.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.
